_transcription: ENGLISH half only. The paper is bilingual with Hindi and English on ALTERNATING pages; the alternating hypothesis HELD — English pages are the EVEN 0-based indices 2..22 (idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions). 23 pages total, 38 questions, 80 marks. Stems transcribed AS PRINTED, never the 'intended' reading. All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the official marking scheme for this exact paper code (65/4/3) — series 65/4's scheme renders every `Ans` row as an IMAGE, so all 20 were read off the rendered MS pages (ms idx 2-6), not grepped and not derived. My own independent derivation agreed with CBSE on all 20; no disagreement to flag. 38 of the 52 rows are questions 65/4/1 also carries (this paper is largely a reshuffle of the same block pool, renumbered in both directions — e.g. this paper's Q2 is 65/4/1's Q10 and its Q10 is 65/4/1's Q2): each was confirmed on MY page and then reused byte-for-byte from data/2025-65-4-1.questions.json, so it dedups at commit rather than shipping a near-duplicate. NOTE FOR THE INDEX: plan.txt listed only 15 blocks as byte-identical and 31 as NEW; the true overlap with 65/4/1 alone is 38 of 52 rows, so its 'TRANSCRIBE' label was a hypothesis in 23 cases — exactly as the brief warns. Only 14 rows are genuinely new relative to 65/4/1: Q1 Q4 Q6 Q7 Q14 Q16 Q21 Q25 Q26 Q29a Q29b Q31 Q34a Q34b. Raised decimal points printed by the paper (47·7) are written {\cdot}. Q26's denominator prints a radical OVER x^{3/2}, i.e. 1 + sqrt(x^{3/2}) rather than the familiar 1 + x^{3/2}; this looked like a misprint and is NOT one — the marking scheme reprints the same form and its worked solution substitutes x^{3/2}=t then sqrt(t)=z, ending at (4/3)[sqrt(x^{3/2}) - log|1+sqrt(x^{3/2})|]+C. Transcribed as printed, no flag. Q31 is the paper's only figure dependency (an LPP feasible-region graph); Q37 and Q38 carry decorative photographs/cartoons only — every number needed is in the stem text — so neither is marked as a figure dependency. FOR THE SOLUTION-AUTHORING STEP: the marking scheme's own A29(a)(ii) is internally wrong — it writes P(X>=1) = 1 - P(X=1) and substitutes p/3, yet prints 7/19, which is 1 - p = 1 - P(X=0). The printed final value 7/19 is correct; the line above it is not. Do not copy that step.

questions.context:
Some students are having a misconception while comparing decimals. For example, a student may mention that \(78{\cdot}56 > 78{\cdot}9\) as 7856 > 789. In order to assess this concept, a decimal comparison test was administered to the students of class VI through the following question :

In the recently held Sports Day in the school, 5 students participated in a javelin throw competition. The distances to which they have thrown the javelin are shown below in the table :

| Name of student | Distance of javelin (in meters) |
|---|---|
| Ajay | \(47{\cdot}7\) |
| Bijoy | \(47{\cdot}07\) |
| Kartik | \(43{\cdot}09\) |
| Dinesh | \(43{\cdot}9\) |
| Devesh | \(45{\cdot}2\) |

The students were asked to identify who has thrown the javelin the farthest.

Based on the test attempted by the students, the teacher concludes that 40% of the students have the misconception in the concept of decimal comparison and the rest do not have the misconception. 80% of the students having misconception answered Bijoy as the correct answer in the paper. 90% of the students who are identified with not having misconception, did not answer Bijoy as their answer.

On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: What is the probability of a student not having misconception but still answers Bijoy in the test ?

questions.context:
During a heavy gaming session, the temperature of a student's laptop processor increases significantly. After the session, the processor begins to cool down, and the rate of cooling is proportional to the difference between the processor's temperature and the room temperature \((25^\circ\text{C})\). Initially the processor's temperature is \(85^\circ\text{C}\). The rate of cooling is defined by the equation \(\frac{d}{dt}(T(t)) = -k(T(t) - 25)\),

where T(t) represents the temperature of the processor at time t (in minutes) and k is a constant.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: Find the expression for temperature of processor, T(t) given that \(T(0) = 85^\circ\text{C}\).
